definition_en: a barrier around a field or garden, the sport of fighting with swords, or to buy and sell stolen goods
core_image: 木栅栏沿着草坡延伸，风吹过时轻轻作响
scene: 院子四周立着一圈木栅栏，风吹过时轻轻作响。A wooden fence surrounds the garden.
sceneCN: 这里 fence 是「栅栏」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一圈木栅栏围着花园。

senses.title: Barrier around land
senses.definition: a barrier of wood, wire, or metal around a field or garden
senses.definitionCN: 围住田地或花园的木、铁丝或金属障碍物
senses.example: A wooden fence surrounds the garden.
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of an enclosure.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示「围合障碍」的日常义。

senses.title: Sport with swords
senses.definition: the sport of fighting with long thin swords
senses.definitionCN: 用细长剑进行的体育运动
senses.example: She trains in fencing twice a week.
senses.why: Fencing is the noun of the sword sport.
senses.whyCN: fencing 是击剑运动的名称。

senses.title: Enclose with a fence
senses.definition: to put a fence around an area
senses.definitionCN: 在某片区域周围设置栅栏
senses.example: They fenced the field to keep sheep in.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把田地围起来以免羊跑出去。
senses.why: The noun supplies a verb for enclosing.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为表示「围起来」的动词。

senses.title: Deal in stolen goods
senses.definition: to buy and sell property that was stolen
senses.definitionCN: 买卖偷来的财物
senses.example: He was arrested for fencing stolen bikes.
senses.why: The criminal sense is older than it looks.
senses.whyCN: 这个犯罪义比看上去更古老。

intro.en: Fence is a shortened form of defence, from Latin defendere, to ward off.
intro.cn: fence 是 defence 的缩略形式，出自拉丁语 defendere（挡开）。

items.en: Defendere meant to ward off or protect.
items.cn: defendere 意为挡开、保护。

items.en: Defens meant defence or protection.
items.cn: defens 意为防御、保护。

items.en: Fens was shortened from defens.
items.cn: fens 由 defens 缩略而来。

items.en: The word came to mean a barrier and the sword sport.
items.cn: 该词逐渐指栅栏与击剑运动。

items.en: Criminals gave fence the sense of dealing in stolen goods.
items.cn: 犯罪圈给 fence 增添了买卖赃物的义项。

note.en: Fence is compared with similar-looking words and with words for barriers.
note.cn: 把 fence 与形近词以及表示障碍物的词作比较。

entries.definition: the sport of fighting with swords
a solid structure that encloses an area

definition_zh: 肥沃的；富饶的；多产的；能生育的
definition_en: of soil, able to produce good crops, of a mind, producing many ideas, or able to have young
core_image: 黑土被犁开，湿润的土块翻起，油亮得发黑
scene: 犁一过，黑油油的泥土翻起来，湿润而松软。The river valley has fertile soil.
sceneCN: 这里 fertile 是「肥沃的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这条河谷拥有肥沃的土壤。

senses.title: Rich soil
senses.definition: of land, able to produce many healthy plants
senses.definitionCN: 土地能长出许多健壮植物
senses.example: The river valley has fertile soil.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河谷拥有肥沃的土壤。
senses.why: This is the basic agricultural sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的农业义。

senses.title: Rich and productive
senses.definition: producing a large amount of something valuable
senses.definitionCN: 出产大量有价值的东西
senses.example: Trade made the region fertile and wealthy.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易让这个地区富饶起来。
senses.why: Land that bears much is called fertile.
senses.whyCN: 出产丰厚的地方也被称作 fertile。

senses.title: Full of ideas
senses.definition: of a mind, producing many ideas
senses.definitionCN: 头脑能产生许多想法
senses.example: She has a fertile imagination.
senses.why: The image of rich soil extends to the mind.
senses.whyCN: 肥沃土壤的意象延伸到头脑。

senses.title: Able to reproduce
senses.definition: able to have young or produce seeds
senses.definitionCN: 能够生育后代或产生种子
senses.example: The eggs remained fertile for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 这些卵在一周内仍能受精发育。
senses.why: Biology uses fertile for the power to reproduce.
senses.whyCN: 生物学用 fertile 表示繁殖能力。

intro.en: Fertile comes from Latin fertilis, from ferre, to bear or carry.
intro.cn: fertile 源自拉丁语 fertilis，出自 ferre（承载、出产）。

items.en: Ferre meant to bear or carry.
items.cn: ferre 意为承载、出产。

items.en: Fertilis meant able to bear fruit.
items.cn: fertilis 意为能结果实的。

items.en: Fertile passed into French with the same sense.
items.cn: fertile 以同样的意义进入法语。

items.en: English fertile described rich land.
items.cn: 英语 fertile 形容肥沃的土地。

items.en: The word spread to minds and to biology.
items.cn: 该词扩展到头脑与生物学领域。

note.en: Fertile is compared with similar-looking words and with words for productivity.
note.cn: 把 fertile 与形近词以及表示丰产的词作比较。

entries.definition: to make soil richer or an egg able to grow
producing a lot of something good

normalIntro.cn: fertile 意为能大量出产生命或想法。

normal.cn: fertile 出自一个意为「承载、出产」的动词。

normal.cn: 肥沃的土壤长出健壮的庄稼。

normal.en: A fertile mind invents many ideas.

normal.en: Fertilizer makes land more fertile.

abstract.en: Fertility is the power to turn one thing into many.
abstract.cn: 丰产，是把一变成多的力量。

abstract.en: A fertile idea feeds other ideas.
abstract.cn: 一个有生命力的想法会滋养别的想法。

abstract.en: Even rich ground needs rest.
abstract.cn: 再肥沃的土地也需要休养。

examples.en: The river valley has fertile soil.
examples.cn: 这条河谷拥有肥沃的土壤。

examples.en: She has a fertile imagination.
examples.cn: 她有丰富的想象力。

examples.en: The eggs remained fertile for a week.
examples.cn: 这些卵在一周内仍能受精发育。

core.en: Able to bear much growth.

branches.en: Soil that gives strong plants.

branches.en: Land that yields wealth.
A mind crowded with ideas.
A body able to produce young.
Rich land and abundant yield belong together.

intro.en: Fertile belongs to the Latin ferre family of bearing words.

definition_zh: 肥料；化肥；促使发展的东西
definition_en: a substance added to soil to help plants grow, especially a chemical product, or something that helps an idea develop
core_image: 白色颗粒从袋口倒进土里，很快被雨水洇湿
scene: 他把一袋白色颗粒均匀撒进田里。Farmers spread fertilizer on the fields.
sceneCN: 这里 fertilizer 是「肥料」（第 1 个义项）；句意：农民把肥料撒在田里。

senses.title: Substance for soil
senses.definition: a substance added to soil to help plants grow
senses.definitionCN: 加入土壤以帮助植物生长的物质
senses.example: Farmers spread fertilizer on the fields.
senses.why: This is the general agricultural sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是通用的农业义。

senses.title: Chemical product
senses.definition: a manufactured chemical product used on crops
senses.definitionCN: 用于农作物的工业化化学产品
senses.example: The factory makes nitrogen fertilizer.
senses.why: Modern farming relies on chemical fertilizers.
senses.whyCN: 现代农业依赖化学肥料。

senses.title: Something that promotes growth
senses.definition: something that helps an idea or process develop
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某种想法或过程发展的东西
senses.example: Praise is fertilizer for young talent.
senses.exampleCN: 赞赏是年轻人才成长的养料。
senses.why: The farming image can describe ideas.
senses.whyCN: 农业意象可以被用来形容想法。

definition_en: a special day or period of celebration, or a series of performances of music, film, or theatre
core_image: 街上挂满红灯笼，鼓声从巷口一路传过来
scene: 整条街挂起红灯笼，鼓声从巷口一路响过来。The whole town joins the spring festival.

senses.title: Arts event

senses.title: Merry celebration

senses.definitionCN: 宴饮与公众欢聚的喜庆场合
senses.example: The street was full of festival cheer.
senses.exampleCN: 街上洋溢着节庆的欢乐。

senses.why: People can be fetched as well as objects.
senses.whyCN: 人也可以像物品一样被「接来」。

senses.title: Sell for a price
senses.definition: to be sold for a particular amount of money
senses.definitionCN: 以某个价钱被卖出
senses.example: The old clock fetched a high price.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧钟卖了个好价钱。
senses.why: An object can fetch what buyers pay for it.
senses.whyCN: 物品能「卖得」买家愿付的价钱。

intro.en: Fetch comes from Old English feccan, to go and get.
intro.cn: fetch 源自古英语 feccan（去取来）。

items.en: Feccan meant to go and bring.
items.cn: feccan 意为去取回。

items.en: The verb appeared in everyday household use.
items.cn: 该动词常见于日常家务语境。

items.en: Fetch kept the idea of a round trip.
items.cn: fetch 保留了「往返一趟」的意思。

items.en: It came to mean to bring a person.
items.cn: 它开始表示把人带来。

items.en: Trade gave it the sense of selling for a price.
items.cn: 商业又赋予它「卖得价钱」的义项。

note.en: Fetch is compared with similar-looking words and with verbs of bringing.
note.cn: 把 fetch 与形近词以及表示「带来」的动词作比较。

entries.definition: to carry something to a place

normalIntro.en: Fetch means to go, get something, and come back.
normalIntro.cn: fetch 意为去、取到手，再回来。

normal.en: Fetch implies a round trip.
normal.cn: fetch 隐含往返一趟。

normal.en: A dog loves to fetch a ball.
normal.cn: 狗喜欢把球叼回来。

normal.en: To fetch a doctor is to go and bring one.
normal.cn: fetch a doctor 就是去把医生请来。

normal.en: A house can fetch a high price.
normal.cn: 房子可以卖个好价钱。

normal.en: Far-fetched means stretched too far to believe.
normal.cn: far-fetched 意为牵强到难以相信。

abstract.en: To fetch is to close a distance and return.
abstract.cn: 去取，就是消除一段距离再回来。

abstract.en: What a thing fetches is what someone will pay.
abstract.cn: 一件东西卖得多少，取决于有人愿付多少。

abstract.en: Some errands are small journeys of care.
abstract.cn: 有些跑腿，是小小的关心之行。

examples.en: The dog fetched the ball.
examples.cn: 狗把球叼了回来。

examples.en: Please fetch the doctor quickly.
examples.cn: 请快去把医生请来。

examples.en: The old clock fetched a high price.
examples.cn: 那座旧钟卖了个好价钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: fetch 是古英语 feccan 的延续，核心是「去一趟再带回来」，由取物引申为接人、卖得价钱。

root: 源自古英语 feccan（去取回），核心义「到别处取来」。

sensesIntro.en: Fetch means to bring something back, to bring a person, or to sell for a price.
sensesIntro.cn: fetch 意为取来、接来或卖得价钱。

core.en: To go, take, and return with something.
core.cn: 去、拿上，再带着东西回来。

branches.en: An object is carried back.
A person is brought to a place.
A sale produces a price.
branches.cn: 一次出售换来一个价钱。

branches.en: Objects and people share the round trip.
branches.cn: 取物与接人都是同一趟往返。

branches.en: The price sense grew from trade.
branches.cn: 价钱义从交易中发展而来。

intro.en: Fetch forms a few compounds, including the common far-fetched.
intro.cn: fetch 构成少量复合词，其中 far-fetched 最常用。

latinIntro.en: This is a Germanic word, so there are no Latin base forms to add.
latinIntro.cn: 这是日耳曼语词，没有对应的拉丁语词根条目。

items.exampleCN: 你能把我的外套拿来吗？

items.example: He fetched a chair for the guest.
items.exampleCN: 他给客人搬来一把椅子。

items.meaning: attractive, or the act of fetching
items.exampleCN: 她戴着一顶迷人的帽子。

items.meaning: a person or thing that fetches
items.example: The dog is a good fetcher.

items.exampleCN: 这个借口听起来很牵强。

items.example: He spent the day on fetch-and-carry tasks.
items.exampleCN: 他一整天都在跑腿打杂。

definition_en: an abnormally high body temperature, a disease that causes it, or a state of great excitement
core_image: 额头贴着退热贴，体温计的红线停在很高的位置
scene: 孩子额头滚烫，母亲连夜守在床边。The child has a high fever.
sceneCN: 这里 fever 是「发烧」（第 1 个义项）；句意：孩子发着高烧。

senses.title: High body temperature
senses.definition: a body temperature that is higher than normal
senses.definitionCN: 高于正常水平的体温
senses.example: The child has a high fever.
senses.why: This is the everyday medical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常医学义。

senses.title: Disease with fever
senses.definition: a disease that causes a high temperature
senses.definitionCN: 引起高体温的疾病
senses.example: The doctor treated a tropical fever.
senses.exampleCN: 医生治疗了一种热带热病。
senses.why: Fever can name the illness itself.
senses.whyCN: fever 可以直接指这种疾病。

senses.title: Great excitement
senses.definition: a state of intense excitement or activity
senses.definitionCN: 极度兴奋或活跃的状态
senses.example: The crowd was in a fever of excitement.
senses.why: The heat of illness became a metaphor for excitement.
senses.whyCN: 疾病的热度被比作情绪的高涨。

intro.en: Fever comes from Latin febris, fever, which passed into Old English as fefor.
intro.cn: fever 源自拉丁语 febris（热病），以 fefor 的形式进入古英语。

items.en: Febris meant fever or a feverish illness.
items.cn: febris 意为发烧或热病。

items.en: Fefor named a high temperature.
items.cn: fefor 指高体温。

items.en: The spelling settled as fever.
items.cn: 拼写逐渐固定为 fever。

items.en: Fever covered both the symptom and the disease.
items.cn: fever 兼指症状与疾病。

items.en: The word gained figurative uses for excitement.
items.cn: 该词获得了表示情绪激动的比喻用法。

note.en: Fever is compared with similar-sounding words and with words for illness and excitement.
note.cn: 把 fever 与近音词以及表示疾病、兴奋的词作比较。

entries.definition: having a fever or acting excitedly
the measured heat of a body

normalIntro.en: Fever means high body heat, a disease that causes it, or heated excitement.
normalIntro.cn: fever 意为高体温、引起发热的疾病，或情绪上的狂热。

normal.en: You run a fever when your body is too hot.
normal.cn: 体温过高时你就是发烧了。

normal.en: Hay fever is an allergy, not an infection.
normal.cn: 花粉热是过敏，不是感染。

normal.en: Fever pitch means the highest excitement.
normal.cn: fever pitch 意为极度兴奋。

normal.en: The adjective is feverish.
normal.cn: 形容词是 feverish。

normal.en: Fever shares a Latin root with febrile.
normal.cn: fever 与 febrile 共享拉丁词根。

abstract.en: Fever is heat that comes from inside.
abstract.cn: 发烧是从身体内部升起的灼热。

abstract.en: Excitement can burn like a fever.
abstract.cn: 兴奋可以像发烧一样灼人。

abstract.en: A fever breaks when the body wins.
abstract.cn: 烧退之时，就是身体赢了。

examples.en: The child has a high fever.
examples.cn: 孩子发着高烧。

examples.en: The doctor treated a tropical fever.
examples.cn: 医生治疗了一种热带热病。

examples.en: The crowd was in a fever of excitement.
examples.cn: 人群陷入狂热的兴奋。

dict_mnemonic.text: fever 源自拉丁语 febris（热病），先指发烧与热病，后引申为情绪上的狂热。

root: 源自拉丁语 febris（热病），核心义「身体内部升起的灼热」。

sensesIntro.en: Fever means a high temperature, a febrile disease, or intense excitement.
sensesIntro.cn: fever 意为发烧、热病或狂热。

core.en: Heat rising beyond the normal level.
core.cn: 超出正常水平的热度。

branches.en: The body is hotter than it should be.
An illness brings the heat.
branches.cn: 某种疾病带来这种高热。

branches.en: A crowd burns with excitement.
The symptom and the disease share a name.
branches.cn: 症状与疾病共用一个名字。

branches.en: Both heats are measured by how they feel.
branches.cn: 两种热度都靠感受来衡量。

intro.en: Fever builds a small family of medical and emotional words.
intro.cn: fever 构成一组表示疾病与情绪的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin febris is the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 febris 是历史词根。

items.exampleCN: 有些发烧不用药也会退。

items.example: He spoke in a fevered voice.

items.meaning: the state of having a fever

items.example: Cabin fever set in after a week of rain.
items.exampleCN: 下了一周雨，人都憋出烦躁了。

definition_en: not many, a small number, or the small group of chosen people
core_image: 空荡的教室里只坐着三四个人，前排还空着
scene: 教室空荡荡的，只坐了三四个人。Few students came to the lecture.
sceneCN: 这里 few 是「很少的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：来听讲座的学生很少。

senses.title: Not many
senses.definition: a small number of people or things
senses.definitionCN: 数量很少的人或物
senses.example: Few students came to the lecture.
senses.why: This is the basic negative quantity sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示数量少的基本否定义。

senses.title: A few
senses.definition: a small but positive number of something
senses.definitionCN: 少量但确实存在的一些
senses.example: A few friends waited outside.
senses.why: Adding a changes the tone from scarce to some.
senses.whyCN: 加上 a 后，语气从「稀少」变为「有一些」。

senses.title: The few
senses.definition: the small group of people who are special or chosen
senses.definitionCN: 特殊或被选出的那一小群人
senses.example: The few who stayed helped clean up.
senses.exampleCN: 留下来的少数人帮忙打扫。
senses.why: With the, few names a select group.
senses.whyCN: 与 the 连用时，few 指特定的一小群人。

intro.en: Few comes from Old English feawe, a Germanic word for a small number.
intro.cn: few 源自古英语 feawe，是日耳曼语中表示「少量」的词。

items.en: Feawe meant not many.
items.cn: feawe 意为不多。

items.en: The word agreed with plural nouns.
items.cn: 该词与复数名词搭配。

items.en: Few settled into its modern spelling.
items.cn: few 固定为现代拼写。

items.en: Fewer and fewest became the comparison forms.
items.cn: fewer 与 fewest 成为比较级和最高级。

items.en: The phrase a few developed a positive sense.
items.cn: 短语 a few 发展出肯定的含义。

note.en: Few is compared with similar-sounding words and with words for scarcity.
note.cn: 把 few 与近音词以及表示稀少的词作比较。

entries.definition: more than two but not many

normalIntro.en: Few means not many, while a few means some.
normalIntro.cn: few 意为很少，而 a few 意为有几个。

normal.en: Few is negative: almost none.
normal.cn: few 带有否定意味：几乎没有。

normal.en: A few is positive: a small number.
normal.cn: a few 带有肯定意味：有几个。

normal.en: Use fewer with countable nouns.
normal.cn: fewer 与可数名词连用。

normal.en: Few and far between means very rare.
normal.cn: few and far between 意为非常稀少。

normal.en: The chosen few are a special small group.
normal.cn: the chosen few 指被选出的少数人。

abstract.en: Few and a few describe the same size differently.
abstract.cn: few 与 a few 用不同眼光描述同样的数量。

abstract.en: Scarcity changes the value of things.
abstract.cn: 稀少会改变事物的价值。

abstract.en: What few remain may matter most.
abstract.cn: 剩下的少数，也许最重要。

examples.en: Few students came to the lecture.
examples.cn: 来听讲座的学生很少。

examples.en: A few friends waited outside.
examples.cn: 几个朋友在外面等着。

examples.en: The few who stayed helped clean up.
examples.cn: 留下来的少数人帮忙打扫。

dict_mnemonic.text: few 是日耳曼语本族词，核心义「数量少」；加 a 后转为肯定，fewer 与 fewest 分别为比较级和最高级。

root: 源自古英语 feawe（不多），属日耳曼语本族词，核心义「数量很少」。

sensesIntro.en: Few means not many, a small number, or the chosen small group.
sensesIntro.cn: few 意为很少、几个或少数人。

core.en: A number smaller than expected.
core.cn: 比预期更小的数量。

branches.en: Almost none came.
Some did come.
A select handful remains.
One word, two attitudes.
Scarcity can make a group special.
branches.cn: 稀少能让一群人显得特别。

intro.en: Few forms a small set of quantity words and phrases.
intro.cn: few 构成少量表示数量的词与短语。

latinIntro.en: This is a Germanic word, so there are no Latin base forms to add.
latinIntro.cn: 这是日耳曼语词，没有对应的拉丁语词根条目。

items.example: The fewness of the guests surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 客人如此之少让我们吃惊。

items.example: A few seats are still free.
Quite a few people signed up.
Good helpers are few and far between.

definition_zh: 纤维；纤维材料；膳食纤维；品格
definition_en: a thin thread-like part of a material, the part of food that helps digestion, or strength of character
core_image: 麻绳被捻开，细丝在光里散成一片
scene: 她把麻绳捻开，露出一缕缕细丝。The rope is made of natural fibre.
sceneCN: 这里 fibre 是「纤维」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这根绳子由天然纤维制成。

senses.title: Thin thread
senses.definition: a thin thread-like part of a natural or artificial material
senses.definitionCN: 天然或人造材料中细线状的部分
senses.example: The rope is made of natural fibre.
senses.exampleCN: 这根绳子由天然纤维制成。
senses.why: This is the basic material sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的材料义。

senses.title: Dietary fibre
senses.definition: the part of plant food that helps digestion
senses.definitionCN: 植物性食物中帮助消化的部分
senses.example: Beans are high in fibre.
senses.why: Food science uses fibre for indigestible plant matter.
senses.whyCN: 食品科学用 fibre 指不可消化的植物成分。

senses.title: Strength of character
senses.definition: the quality of strong moral character
senses.definitionCN: 坚强的道德品格
senses.example: The crisis tested the moral fibre of the town.
senses.exampleCN: 这场危机考验了全镇的道德品格。
senses.why: The image of tough threads became a moral metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 坚韧纤维的意象被用作道德比喻。

intro.en: Fibre comes from Latin fibra, a thread or filament, through French fibre.
intro.cn: fibre 源自拉丁语 fibra（细线、纤维），经法语 fibre 进入英语。

items.en: Fibra meant a thread or fine filament.
items.cn: fibra 意为细线、纤维。

items.en: Fibre kept the same material sense.
items.cn: 法语 fibre 保留了相同的材料义。

items.en: English fibre described threads in plants and cloth.
items.cn: 英语 fibre 指植物与织物中的细丝。

items.en: Industry added glass and carbon fibres.
items.cn: 工业领域增加了玻璃纤维与碳纤维。

items.en: Medicine and ethics gave it new uses.
items.cn: 医学与伦理学又赋予它新的用法。

note.en: Fibre is compared with similar-looking words and with words for threads.
note.cn: 把 fibre 与形近词以及表示细线的词作比较。

entries.definition: a thin line of spun fibre

normalIntro.en: Fibre means a thin thread, the rough part of food, or moral strength.
normalIntro.cn: fibre 意为细纤维、食物中的纤维，或道德品格。

normal.en: Natural fibres come from plants or animals.
normal.cn: 天然纤维来自植物或动物。

normal.en: Vegetables are high in fibre.
normal.cn: 蔬菜富含纤维。

normal.en: Carbon fibre is strong and light.
normal.cn: 碳纤维又强又轻。

normal.en: Fibre optics carry light through glass threads.
normal.cn: 光纤让光在玻璃丝中传输。

normal.en: Moral fibre means strength of character.
normal.cn: moral fibre 意为品格的力量。

abstract.en: Many thin threads together make a strong rope.
abstract.cn: 许多细丝合在一起就成了结实的绳。

abstract.en: What cannot be digested can still keep the body well.
abstract.cn: 无法消化的东西，也能让身体保持良好。

abstract.en: Character, like cloth, is woven thread by thread.
abstract.cn: 品格如布，是一缕一缕织成的。

examples.en: The rope is made of natural fibre.
examples.cn: 这根绳子由天然纤维制成。

examples.en: Beans are high in fibre.
examples.cn: 豆类富含膳食纤维。

examples.en: The crisis tested the moral fibre of the town.
examples.cn: 这场危机考验了全镇的道德品格。

dict_mnemonic.text: fibre 源自拉丁语 fibra（细丝），由材料纤维引申到膳食纤维，再比喻为道德品格。

root: 源自拉丁语 fibra（细线、纤维），核心义「细长的一缕」。

sensesIntro.en: Fibre means a thin thread, dietary fibre, or strength of character.
sensesIntro.cn: fibre 意为纤维、膳食纤维或品格。

core.en: A fine strand of material.
core.cn: 材料中细细的一缕。

branches.en: A single thin strand.
Many strands woven into cloth.
The plant matter that aids digestion.
Inner strength pictured as tough thread.
branches.cn: 被比作坚韧丝线的内在力量。

branches.en: Material and moral strength share one image.
branches.cn: 物质与道德的坚韧共享同一意象。

intro.en: Fibre forms compounds for glass, optics, and character.
intro.cn: fibre 可构成玻璃纤维、光纤、品格等复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fibra is the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fibra 是历史词根。

definition_zh: 小说；虚构作品；编造的说法
definition_en: stories about imaginary people and events, an invented story, or something that is not true
core_image: 书页间夹着一张手绘地图，海岸线全是虚构的
scene: 她合上小说，久久没从那个虚构的世界里出来。The story is a work of fiction.
sceneCN: 这里 fiction 是「虚构作品」（第 2 个义项）；句意：这个故事是一部虚构作品。

senses.title: Stories as a genre
senses.definition: books and stories about imaginary people and events
senses.definitionCN: 关于想象中人物与事件的书和故事
senses.example: She writes fiction for young readers.
senses.why: This is the literary category sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是文学门类义。

senses.title: Invented story
senses.definition: a single story or work that is invented rather than factual
senses.definitionCN: 单个虚构而非纪实的故事或作品
senses.example: The story is a work of fiction.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事是一部虚构作品。
senses.why: One specific work can be called a fiction.
senses.whyCN: 单独一部作品也可以称为 fiction。

senses.title: False claim
senses.definition: something that is untrue and presented as fact
senses.definitionCN: 被当作事实说出的不真实之事
senses.example: The report was pure fiction.
senses.why: Outside literature, fiction means a falsehood.
senses.whyCN: 在文学之外，fiction 指虚假的说法。

intro.en: Fiction comes from Latin fictio, a shaping or invention, from fingere, to shape.
intro.cn: fiction 源自拉丁语 fictio（塑造、编造），出自 fingere（塑造）。

items.en: Fingere meant to shape or mold.
items.cn: fingere 意为塑造、捏制。

items.en: Fictio meant a shaping or invention.
items.cn: fictio 意为塑造、虚构。

items.en: Fiction passed into French as an invented story.
items.cn: fiction 以「编造的故事」之义进入法语。

items.en: English fiction meant something invented.
items.cn: 英语 fiction 意为编造之物。

items.en: The word became the name of a literary kind.
items.cn: 该词成为一类文学体裁的名称。

note.en: Fiction is compared with similar-looking words and with words for stories and falsehood.
note.cn: 把 fiction 与形近词以及表示故事、虚假的词作比较。

entries.definition: to turn real events into fiction
a told or written account of events
something made up in the mind

normalIntro.en: Fiction is something shaped by the imagination rather than found in fact.
normalIntro.cn: fiction 是想象塑造出来的东西，而非事实。

normal.en: Fiction and fact are opposites.
normal.cn: fiction 与 fact 相对。

normal.en: Science fiction imagines future technology.
normal.cn: 科幻小说想象未来科技。

normal.en: A fictional character never really lived.
normal.cn: 虚构人物从未真实存在。

normal.en: Nonfiction tells about real events.
normal.cn: 非虚构作品讲述真实事件。

normal.en: Calling a report fiction means it is made up.
normal.cn: 说一份报告是 fiction，就是说是编的。

abstract.en: Fiction tells the truth through invented people.

normal.en: Figure out means to find the answer.
normal.cn: figure out 意为找到答案。

normal.en: A figure can be a drawing in a book.
normal.cn: figure 可以是书中的插图。

normal.en: She keeps her figure by walking.
normal.cn: 她靠走路保持身材。

abstract.en: A shape becomes a number once we count it.
abstract.cn: 一旦我们去数，形状就变成数字。

abstract.en: A person can be a figure in history.
abstract.cn: 一个人可以成为历史中的一个人物。

abstract.en: To figure is to give shape to a thought.
abstract.cn: 去推断，就是给想法一个形状。

examples.en: The figures show a steady rise.
examples.cn: 图表上的数字稳步上升。

examples.en: She is a public figure.
examples.cn: 她是一位公众人物。

examples.en: I figure it will rain today.
examples.cn: 我估计今天会下雨。

dict_mnemonic.text: figure 出自拉丁语 figura（形状），本义「塑造出的形态」，由图形扩展到数字、人物、身材与推断。

root: 源自拉丁语 figura（形状），出自 fingere（塑造），核心义「成形的样子」。

sensesIntro.en: Figure means a number, a person, a shape, a body form, or to think and calculate.
sensesIntro.cn: figure 意为数字、人物、图形、身材，或认为与估算。

core.en: A form that can be seen, counted, or thought about.
core.cn: 可以被看见、被计数或被思考的形态。

branches.en: Data expressed as numbers.
A person who stands out.
A drawn or printed shape.
The outline of a body.
The act of concluding.

intro.en: Figure belongs to the Latin family of shaping and form.
intro.cn: figure 属于拉丁语中表示塑造与形状的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin figura and fingere are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 figura 与 fingere 是历史词根。

items.example: The president is only a figurehead.
items.exampleCN: 这位总统只是名义领袖。
那个故事是臆造出来的。

definition_zh: 文件；档案；归档；排队行进
definition_en: a folder or set of papers, a collection of stored information, to store papers in order, or to walk in a line
core_image: 一叠纸被一根细线穿在一起，挂在墙上的钉子上
scene: 他打开文件，读起第一页。He opened the file and read the first page.
sceneCN: 这里 file 是「文件」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他打开文件，读起第一页。

senses.title: Document
senses.definition: a set of papers or data kept together
senses.definitionCN: 归在一起的一组纸质或电子资料
senses.example: He opened the file and read the first page.
senses.exampleCN: 他打开文件，读起第一页。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of a document.
senses.whyCN: 这是文件最常见的意思。

senses.title: Stored record
senses.definition: a collection of records kept for reference
senses.definitionCN: 供查阅的档案记录
senses.example: The police keep the case on file.
senses.why: Records are kept in a file for later use.
senses.whyCN: 记录被存进档案以备日后使用。

senses.title: To store in order
senses.definition: to put papers into a system or place
senses.definitionCN: 把文件放入系统或位置
senses.example: File the reports before Friday.
senses.why: The noun turns into the act of keeping it.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为保存它的动作。

senses.title: To walk in line
senses.definition: to walk one behind another
senses.definitionCN: 一个接一个地走
senses.example: The children filed into the hall.
senses.why: A line of people resembles a string of papers.
senses.whyCN: 一列人就像一串文件。

intro.en: File comes from Latin filum, a thread, because papers were once strung on a line.
intro.cn: file 出自拉丁语 filum（线），因为旧时文件被穿在线上。

items.en: Filum meant a thread or string.
items.cn: filum 意为线或细绳。

items.en: Filare meant to spin thread.
items.cn: filare 意为纺线。

items.en: Filer meant to string papers on a line.
items.cn: filer 意为把文件穿在线上。

items.en: A file became a set of papers kept in order.
items.cn: file 变成按顺序保存的一组文件。

items.en: The word extended to computer files.
items.cn: 该词扩展到计算机文件。

note.en: File is compared with similar-looking words and with words for stored records.
note.cn: 把 file 与形近词以及表示存档记录的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: File is a thread of papers, a stored record, and a line of people.
normalIntro.cn: file 是一串纸、一份存档，也是一列人。

normal.en: Keep the contract on file.
normal.cn: 把合同存档。

normal.en: She filed the letters by date.
normal.cn: 她按日期给信件归档。

normal.en: The students walked in single file.
normal.cn: 学生们排成一列行走。

normal.en: A filename names a computer file.
normal.cn: 文件名给电脑文件命名。

normal.en: File a complaint means to report it formally.
normal.cn: file a complaint 意为正式提出投诉。

abstract.en: A thread can hold many pages into one story.
abstract.cn: 一根线能把许多页穿成一个故事。

abstract.en: Order is what turns paper into a file.
abstract.cn: 秩序把纸张变成档案。

abstract.en: A line of people moves at the speed of its first step.
abstract.cn: 一列人的速度取决于第一步。

examples.en: He opened the file and read the first page.
examples.cn: 他打开文件，读起第一页。

examples.en: The police keep the case on file.
examples.cn: 警方把此案存档。

examples.en: The children filed into the hall.
examples.cn: 孩子们排队走进大厅。

dict_mnemonic.text: file 出自拉丁语 filum（线），本义「把文件穿在线上保存」，后引申为文件、档案与排队行进。

root: 源自拉丁语 filum（线），核心义「用线串起、成序保存」。

sensesIntro.en: File means a document, a stored record, the act of storing, or walking in a line.
sensesIntro.cn: file 意为文件、档案、归档或排队行进。

core.en: Papers held together in order.
core.cn: 按顺序归拢在一起的纸张。

branches.en: Papers kept together.
Records kept for later use.
The act of putting papers away.
People moving one behind another.
A single file and a case file share one word.
branches.cn: 一份文件与一宗案卷共用一个词。

intro.en: File belongs to the Latin thread family, from which profile and filament also come.
intro.cn: file 属于拉丁语「线」词族，profile 与 filament 也出自这里。

latinIntro.en: Latin filum and filare are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 filum 与 filare 是历史词根。

items.example: The files are in the drawer.
The profile shows a smiling face.

definition_en: to make something full, to close a gap, to make someone feel a strong emotion, or to take a role
core_image: 水从壶口倾下，杯子一寸寸被注满
scene: 她把杯子倒满了水。She filled the glass with water.
sceneCN: 这里 filled 是「装满」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她把杯子倒满了水。

senses.title: Make full
senses.definition: to put something into a container until it is full
senses.definitionCN: 往容器里放东西直到满
senses.example: She filled the glass with water.
senses.why: This is the basic sense of making full.
senses.whyCN: 这是使某物变满的基本义。

senses.title: Fill a gap
senses.definition: to close or complete an empty space
senses.definitionCN: 堵住或补全空白
senses.example: Workers filled the hole with cement.
senses.why: A hole is an empty space to be filled.
senses.whyCN: 洞就是等待填满的空处。

senses.title: Full of feeling
senses.definition: to make someone feel a strong emotion
senses.definitionCN: 使人产生强烈情感
senses.example: The news filled her with joy.
senses.exampleCN: 这个消息让她满心欢喜。
senses.why: Emotion can fill a person like water.
senses.whyCN: 情感能像水一样充满一个人。

senses.title: Take a role
senses.definition: to take a position or do a job
senses.definitionCN: 担任职位或从事工作
senses.example: She filled the empty seat on the board.
senses.exampleCN: 她补上了董事会的空缺席位。
senses.why: A vacant role is a space to be filled.
senses.whyCN: 空缺的职位就是一个待填的位置。

intro.en: Fill comes from Old English fyllan, to make full, from full.
intro.cn: fill 源自古英语 fyllan（使满），出自 full。

items.en: Full meant having no empty space.
items.cn: full 意为没有空隙。

items.en: Fyllan meant to make something full.
items.cn: fyllan 意为使某物变满。

items.en: Fillen covered containers and holes.
items.cn: fillen 既指装满容器也指填洞。

items.en: Fill in and fill out name the act of completing forms.
items.cn: 英语中用 fill in 与 fill out 表示填写表格。

items.en: Refill means to fill again.
items.cn: refill 意为重新装满。

note.en: Fill is compared with similar-looking words and with words for loading a space.
note.cn: 把 fill 与形近词以及表示装入空间的词作比较。

entries.definition: to put things into a container
to take up a space or role

normalIntro.en: Fill means to make full, close a gap, flood with feeling, or take a role.
normalIntro.cn: fill 意为装满、填补、充满情感或担任。

normal.en: Fill the bottle with clean water.
normal.cn: 把瓶子装满干净的水。

normal.en: Fill in the form in black ink.
normal.cn: 用黑色墨水填写表格。

normal.en: A good meal fills the room with warmth.
normal.cn: 一顿好饭让满屋温暖。

normal.en: She filled the role of guide.
normal.cn: 她担任了向导的角色。

normal.en: Refill means to fill the cup again.
normal.cn: refill 意为再把杯子装满。

abstract.en: A hole is a chance for something to fill it.
abstract.cn: 空洞正是某物来填补的机会。

abstract.en: Feeling can fill a room without a sound.
abstract.cn: 情感可以无声地充满房间。

abstract.en: A role waits to be filled by someone willing.
abstract.cn: 一个角色等着愿意的人来担任。

examples.en: She filled the glass with water.
examples.cn: 她把杯子倒满了水。

examples.en: Workers filled the hole with cement.
examples.cn: 工人用水泥填平了洞。

examples.en: The news filled her with joy.
examples.cn: 这个消息让她满心欢喜。

dict_mnemonic.text: fill 源自古英语 fyllan（使满），出自 full，本义「使容器变满」，后扩展为填补、充满情感与担任。

root: 源自古英语 fyllan（使满），出自 full，核心义「使变满」。

sensesIntro.en: Fill means to make full, close a gap, overwhelm with feeling, or take a role.
sensesIntro.cn: fill 意为装满、填补、充满或担任。

core.en: Empty space becoming full.
core.cn: 空处被填满。

branches.en: A container reaching its limit.
An empty space closed up.
Emotion rising to the brim.
A position taken by someone.
What makes full also makes whole.

intro.en: Fill belongs to the Germanic full family.
intro.cn: fill 属于日耳曼语中表示「满」的词族。

latinIntro.en: Fill has no Latin ancestor; Latin plenus and implere are semantic parallels.
latinIntro.cn: fill 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 plenus 与 implere 只是语义对应。

items.meaning: the act or something that fills
items.example: The filling is made of fruit.
